rows.name: Windows plugin initialization and cache failures

brief.what_changed: Windows plugin initialization and cache failure reports increased from 5 to 6 issues in the current period, with the cluster maintaining a normal growth trajectory at a 20% raw growth rate and 0.04 percentage-point share increase.
brief.evidence_summary: Multiple high-severity reports describe Windows Chrome/native-host plugin initialization failures and Trusted RPC dependency errors preventing browser agent control (#41358, #42238, #40774). Several issues tie failures to app auto-updates breaking Trusted RPC paths (#40411, #41764) and stale configuration left behind after clean reinstalls (#40357, #41781). At least one macOS report (#40307) suggests the plugin bundling or integrity problem may extend beyond Windows.
brief.affected_workflow: Browser plugin initialization and RPC-based in-app browser control
brief.product_hypothesis: App auto-updates on Windows may be leaving stale or mismatched plugin/cache state and trusted-path configurations, causing subsequent browser plugin initialization and RPC calls to fail until the user manually clears entries or reinstalls.
brief.suggested_validation: 1. Reproduce the failure by performing a clean install, triggering an auto-update cycle, and checking whether chrome-native-hosts entries and trusted-path configs remain consistent. 2. Compare plugin file integrity (e.g., browser-client.mjs presence and version) before and after an update to verify bundling correctness.
brief.recommended_investigation: 1. Audit the Windows auto-update code path to identify whether stale native-host registry entries or cache files are being carried over or improperly updated. 2. Trace the Trusted RPC path resolution logic to determine under what configuration-mismatch conditions it rejects otherwise valid paths.

rows.name: Browser control session hangs and timeouts

brief.what_changed: Reported browser control session hangs and timeouts decreased slightly from 7 to 6 issues in the current period, with a -14% raw growth rate and a -0.16 percentage point share delta, indicating this cluster remains stable rather than expanding.
brief.evidence_summary: Members report that while initial browser connection or tab listing may succeed, subsequent interactive commands like claimTab, tabs.get, DOM reads, or screenshots consistently hang or time out. This occurs across multiple platforms, as seen in issues #40352 (Windows, tabs.get hang), #40358 (macOS, CDP input timeout), and #41494 (macOS, Runtime.evaluate timeout). High severity indicates these failures block core automation workflows.
brief.affected_workflow: Browser automation and interactive tab control
brief.product_hypothesis: The persistent timeouts after initial successful connections may indicate a race condition or stale state in the browser control session management layer, where the communication channel becomes unresponsive to higher-level commands.
brief.suggested_validation: 1. Create a reproducible test case that mimics the sequence of a successful tab listing followed by an interactive command like DOM read to isolate the failure condition. 2. Implement enhanced logging at the boundary between the extension backend and the CDP command layer to capture the exact point of communication breakdown.
brief.affected_surface_platform: Codex App on macOS and Windows, interacting with Chrome and Edge browsers
brief.recommended_investigation: 1. Analyze the browser control session lifecycle logs for issues where basic tab listing succeeds but interactive commands fail, to identify where the command pipeline breaks. 2. Compare the timing and state of CDP connections across the different timeout patterns reported (e.g., DOM/screenshot vs. tab control) to check for common failure points.
